prompt: A chess learner practises only one opening against the same app setting. In a real game, a different opening leaves him lost in the first ten moves. What practice change best builds transferable skill?

options.text: Practise that one opening for even more hours
Vary practice: different openings and positions, so he learns underlying principles rather than one memorised sequence
Only play games he is certain to win
Memorise a second single opening in exactly the same way

explanation: Narrow, identical practice builds a fragile sequence that breaks when conditions change. Varied practice forces the learner to recognise principles across situations, which transfers to new games.
